title: Clara Haskil's birth chart
metaDescription: Clara Haskil's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 16.9° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Three of the nine placements whose signs are settled fall in cardinal signs, the widest weighting the unknown hour leaves certain. The cardinal signs begin things; a chart weighted there treats every stall as a starting gun.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 16.9° into Capricorn — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Venus. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 15.3° Capricorn, Venus at 26.0° Capricorn, Mars at 2.9° Taurus. Mercury in a earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Venus in a earth sign reads as attraction that grows by reliability; Mars in a earth sign reads as effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun conjunction Mercury, 1.7° of separation. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, the Sun sextile Uranus at 2.0°, and Mars opposition Saturn at 3.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mars in Taurus at 2.9° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Gemini at 29.2° is in detriment. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 earth, 3 air, 2 water by element and 3 cardinal, 3 fixed, 3 mutable by modality. Earth signs hold the scheme’s slow end, where results are measured in what survives rather than what starts. No settled placement falls in fire — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 13.8° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
